lots.dropped_entries: Dropped: Gumtree Tasmania entry ($1,250 pair, $200) because gumtree.com.au returned HTTP 403 and it was snippet only. Tasmanian Specialty Timbers ($9,200 etc) because the URL is now a parked domain with no listing. Buy Tasmanian Timbers bird's-eye slabs ($4,000 to $12,000; page opened, $12,000 giant bird's-eye confirmed) as not comparable: exhibition-grade figured slabs versus a plain rough slab. The researcher's April to July 2026 median ($50) is folded into the overall Gowans entry. The researcher's doubt about species is not supported: last week's lots 1113 to 1117 (same pale straw look, same supplier batch) sold as Huon with 4 to 7 bids each, and freshly sawn Huon is often pale straw before it ages to gold.
lots.key_photo_findings: Chalk '1114 16/10/26'. Clearly the widest slab in its row, about the same size and colour as last week's lots 1113 to 1117 (which sold $90 to $155). Pale straw, plain figure, a few small pin knots. Bark-lined void and bark pocket at the top 600 mm, a short check below the chalk date, live edge both sides.
lots.condition: Rough-sawn, air-dried or green (unknown), not flattened. Bark inclusions and a void in the top section reduce usable length; some edge checks.
lots.question_for_gowans: Please give length, width at each end and thickness, and confirm it is Huon pine (a fresh scratch should smell of Huon oil) and whether it is air-dried or green.

lots.condition: Rough-sawn, not flattened, voids and cracks would need epoxy filling; drying state unknown (mango is prone to checking and borer).
lots.question_for_gowans: Is this slab dry (air- or kiln-dried) and free of borer, and are the chalked sizes (850 x 1200 x 45mm) correct?
